We have absolutely loved The Wharf. It is very much a happy place!
The staff are all so kind and welcoming.
Your nursery outshone the other nurseries by a long way!
Our child has grown in confidence this year and loved all of the learning opportunities he has been given!
We couldn’t have wished for a more caring, fun and inspiring place for our children.
Being a young parent I struggle with anxiety and I can’t recommend The Wharf more…the staff have been amazing with me and my daughter.
They don’t just put the kids first but they care for the parents as well.
The teachers are all approachable and always listen if you have any concerns.
It meant the world to me to know I could leave my children with people I could trust and know they were receiving an outstanding early childhood education.
Our son has blossomed while at the wharf.
At the Wharf they are not a team, but rather, they are a family.
We feel as though our son has thrived emotionally, socially and academically since being at the Wharf. We are thrilled at how he has developed and progressed - thank you!
Our son adored his time at the Wharf Nursery School, we wish he could stay another year!
My daughter keeps asking to go to Nursery every day... I think that says it all!
Exceptional. We couldn't ask for a better Nursery!
A truly fantastic place! She has had the most amazing 2 years at The Wharf. I couldn't ask for more!
Welcome
Welcome to The Wharf Nursery School. We are a well-established, maintained (state-funded) nursery school which has been at the heart of the community in Godalming since it was founded in 1947.
Our nursery sessions are for 2 to 5-year-olds from 9am to 3pm/3.30pm, term-time only.
We offer all 3-4 year-olds their 15 hours of nursery school entitlement free of charge. We do not charge top-up fees. Subject to availability of spaces, we offer an additional free 15 hours to those families who are eligible according to government criteria. See 30 hours free childcare - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk) for more information on who is eligible.
Our aim is to help our children become well-motivated, confident and positive individuals. We do this by providing high-quality care and education in a safe, happy and stimulating environment.
Click here for our Virtual Tour.
If you would like to view the nursery in person please call for an appointment.
We hope you can find what you need on our website. If you have any queries please contact us.

Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEN/D)
At The Wharf Nursery School, we celebrate each child as an individual, always seeking to look for children's strengths and to build on the experiences that they start Nursery with.
We recognise that children may have a unique way of communicating and engaging with others. Some children may have a diagnosis or already be on a pathway to this by the time they join us. We firmly believe that parents know their children best and we see them as part of our team in identifying and supporting children at every stage.
We have a qualified teacher as our SENCO (Special Educational Needs Coordinator). It is their job to work alongside the child's family, Key Person and members of our SEN/D team. We work together to help children to settle, integrate into our setting and progress at their own rate through carefully planned experiences.
For the majority of each session children are supported to play and learn alongside their friends. The children also have use of a designated room which is used for individual and small group work sessions. We also have a large garden, a sensory room and a soft play, where children enjoy exploring an exciting array of resources especially designed to help with coordination and concentration.
We work very closely with educational psychologists and other professionals such as speech and language therapists, occupational therapists, physiotherapists and other relevant specialists in order to achieve the best we can for each child.
We know that early intervention for children is key in supporting them to have the best outcomes. Therefore, we encourage parents and carers to engage with us at the earliest opportunity about any concerns that they have in relation to their child's development. Often this is before a child starts in Nursery, as this helps us to plan for their needs. A good way to meet us to discuss these, is through our Stay and Play sessions, which take place on a Wednesday and Thursday here at The Wharf. Alternatively, you can always phone to make an appointment to meet Zoe Bray (Headteacher), or Penny Macland (SENCO). We are always happy to help.
Please feel free to come and talk to us if you have any questions.
Our SEND Co-ordinator: Penny Macland email: senco@wharf.surrey.sch.uk
Please see below for our SEND Information Report and SEND Policy which outline how we support children with additional needs in more detail.
Our Stages of Support, also below, gives examples of how we support the learning needs of all our children.

Nursery School
The Wharf Nursery School is a well-established state-funded nursery school which has been at the heart of the community in Godalming since it was founded in 1947. It was rated as "outstanding" by Ofsted in the last inspection in June 2023. Click here for full Ofsted Report.
Our teaching is based on the Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum. We put particular emphasis on children’s social and emotional development and on fostering their language and their physical skills and independence. These provide the foundations for all their later learning. See How Children Learn at The Wharf for more details.
All classroom staff are qualified and experienced early years teachers and nursery nurses. We also have a strong reputation for our work with children with additional needs, led by our SENCO, and work closely with other professionals and organisations to support all our children and families.
Children usually start in the term after their third birthday. We provide 15 hours of free nursery education for 3- and 4-year-olds and do not charge top-up fees.
We accept some children for government-funded 30-hour places: Monday - Friday 9am - 3pm. See Nursery Sessions and Lunch Club.
We also have a small group of 2-year-olds. Places within this group are either FEET-funded or fee-paying.
Our opening times are 9am - 3.30pm, Monday to Friday, term-time only.
For more information about our nursery sessions see Nursery Sessions and Lunch Club. Please see Admissions for how to apply.
Our Ofsted report in June 2023 says:
“Children truly thrive in this Nursery. They love to learn. Leaders are passionate about ensuring that children have every opportunity to achieve their very best. Relationships are incredibly warm and caring. Staff really nurture the children in their care. They comfort children who are sad or upset to help them to calm down. At this Nursery, all children, including those with special educational needs and/or disabilities, achieve exceptionally well.”
Please see full Ofsted report below.

Nursery Sessions
Children usually start nursery in the term after their third birthday and are then entitled to 15 hours of free education per week. We do not charge top-up fees.
Most children attend for 2½ days a week in one of the following classes:
Green Rockets: Monday 8.55am – 2.55pm, Tuesday 8.55am – 2.55pm, Wednesday 8.55am – 11.55am
Blue Rockets: Wednesday 12.30pm – 3.30pm, Thursday 8.55am – 2.55pm, Friday 8.55am –2.55pm
We accept children for government-funded 30-hour places under the Working Parent Eligibility Scheme. (We can also accept privately funded children.)
This group (Yellow Rockets) runs on Monday - Friday 9.05am - 3.05pm. To find out if you are eligible, please click here for the government website, and let us know if you are eligible when applying for a nursery place.
We also offer places to children in the term after their second birthday. As this is only a small group, (Little Stars) places are limited. These places are either fee-paying or are funded through the Two-year-old funding scheme or the Working Parents Eligibility scheme. Please click here for more information about funding.
Little Stars: Monday - Friday: 9am - 12noon.
Some 15-hour spaces are available. (Mon & Tue 9am - 3pm, Wed 9am - 12pm)
Children staying all day are given a cooked lunch. The cost for lunch is currently £2.90 per day.

The Early Years Pupil Premium
Since April 2015, nurseries, schools, childminders and other childcare providers have been able to claim extra funding through the Early Years Pupil Premium to support children’s development, learning and care.
We can use the extra funding in any way we choose to improve the quality of the early year’s education that we provide for an eligible child. This could include for example additional training for our staff on early language, investing in partnership working with our colleagues in the area to further our expertise or supporting our staff in working on specialised areas such as speech and language.
It is well documented that high quality early education can influence how well a child does at both primary and secondary school so we want to make the most of this additional funding. You may be aware if you have older children that a pupil premium has been available for school age children and it has proved to have given a real boost to the children receiving the funding. We want to do the same for our early years children entitled to this funding.
